weeks.note: Pick loads you could lift 3 more times; own the technique and log every set as your baseline.
Same loads, add reps inside the range; once every set hits the top at RIR 3, add the smallest increment.
Move to RIR 2: same loads should now give 1-2 more reps; progress load when all sets reach the top of the range.
Keep double progression going; last week before accessory rotation, so note which accessories stalled.
Main lifts may go to RIR 1; swap in new accessory variations and add 1 accessory set only if the session still fits the time.
Chase a rep or load PR on each main lift at RIR 1; the extra accessory set is optional on busy weeks.
Last hard week: best reps on main lifts at RIR 1, drop the extra accessory set so you reach the deload fresh.
Half the sets (round up), same weights, RIR 3; keep steps and sleep high, then restart week 1 with heavier baselines.

periodization.progressionRule: Double progression: work inside the rep range at the week's RIR. When every set of an exercise reaches the top of the range at or above the target RIR, add the smallest step next session (dumbbell +2 kg, bar +5 kg, machine +1 plate) and drop back to the bottom of the range. If reps fall below the range two sessions in a row, reduce load ~10% and rebuild. If a session feels unusually heavy (bad sleep, baby night), keep the load and stop at RIR 3: that still counts.

undulation.Strength C – heavier: heavy: 6-8 reps, longest rests (main lifts only may reach RIR 1 from week 5)
undulation.why: Daily undulation spreads stress across the week and is at least as effective as linear models; in volume-equated studies periodization helps strength slightly but does not change hypertrophy (Moesgaard 2022).

rotation.rule: Main lifts (the fixed list) stay the same for the full 8-week block so progress is measurable; change a main lift only at the start of a new block and only if it has stalled for 2+ weeks or causes joint pain, choosing an alternate within +/-1 level of the same pattern. Accessories (face pull, curls, triceps, lateral raise, core, power and conditioning items) rotate every 4 weeks, at week 5 and at week 1 of the next block, to the next alternate of the same pattern and similar level; rotate at most 1-2 exercises per session, restart the new variation at RIR 3 for its first session, and never rotate randomly session to session. Busy-station swaps on the day do not count as a rotation: log them, but return to the planned exercise next session.
rotation.evidence: Systematic variation can broaden regional hypertrophy while excessive/random rotation can blunt gains (Kassiano 2022); varying exercises gave similar strength and size with better motivation (Baz-Valle 2019).

express.keepSlots: Strength days: keep the A and B superset slots (the 4 compound lifts; on Strength C keep A, B1 and B2) and drop C and D. Wednesday: 20 min steady cardio + Dead bug and Side plank. Friday: slams + box jumps (3 sets each) + 4 bike intervals.
rules: Warm-up shrinks to 5 min: 2-3 min easy cardio, then 1 light ramp set of the first lift (skip the mobility list).

Do the kept slots as antagonist supersets (e.g. A1 squat + A2 press, B1 pull + B2 hinge): set of A1, ~45 s, set of A2, then 90 s before the next round. Paired supersets cut session time roughly in half with similar volume (Iversen 2021; Weakley 2017).
2 hard working sets per slot at the week's RIR target (never below RIR 1). If you have 5 spare minutes, give the first lift of the day a 3rd set.
Drop all C/D accessories first; if time remains, add ONE 2-set superset finisher (e.g. lateral raise + hammer curl) with 45 s rest.
Keep the same loads as a full session; Express cuts sets, not weight. Intensity, not volume, is what maintains strength (Spiering 2021).
Rest-pause option for the last set of an accessory: reach the RIR target, rest 15 s, do 2-4 more reps once. Use only on machines/cables, not on squats or deadlifts.
Cooldown is 2 min of walking; stretch later at home if possible.
Two Express sessions give each big muscle ~4+ hard sets per week, the minimum Iversen 2021 suggests for continued gains; three Express sessions give ~6.

busyWeek.why: The three full-body strength sessions train every major muscle 3x per week, which keeps weekly hard sets per muscle around 6-9 (enough to keep progressing as an intermediate-beginner; Schoenfeld 2017, Iversen 2021). Cardio and conditioning are the easiest to replace outside the gym with steps, pram walks and a short home interval, and missing them for a week costs little fitness (Spiering 2021). Space them with a rest day between if possible (e.g. Tue/Thu/Sat). If only 2 sessions are possible, keep Strength A and Strength C (both include squat or hinge, press and pull), run them as Express, and keep daily steps.
busyWeek.ifOnlyOne: Do Strength A as Express: 1 session per week with 1-2 hard sets per exercise at the same load maintains strength and muscle for months (Spiering 2021; Bickel 2011).

homeFallback.name: Goblet squat (one dumbbell; bodyweight squat if none)
Push-up (hands on a sofa or bench to make easier)
One-arm dumbbell row (hand on a chair)
Dumbbell reverse lunge (bodyweight if no dumbbells)

homeFallbackNote: Circuit, about 15 min: do the first 4 moves back-to-back with no rest, rest 60 s, repeat for 3 rounds; then 2 rounds of lunge + dead bug if time allows. Stop each set at RIR 2. This counts as a strength session in the log.
parentTips: Sleep is part of the program: aim for 7+ hours, and use naps to catch up. In a calorie deficit, short sleep (5.5 h) shifted weight loss from fat to lean mass and raised hunger (Nedeltcheva 2010). After a bad night, still train but use Express and RIR 3: no PR attempts.

Most fat-loss movement is outside the gym: walk with the pram or baby carrier, take calls standing, and aim for 7,000-10,000 steps. Non-exercise activity can differ by hundreds of kcal a day between people (Levine 2005), and mortality risk keeps falling with more daily steps up to roughly 6,000-8,000 for adults over 60 and 8,000-10,000 for younger adults (Paluch 2022).

A missed week is not lost progress. One or two short sessions a week at the same weights keep strength and muscle for months (Spiering 2021; Bickel 2011), so on chaotic weeks aim for 'two Express sessions', not 'all or nothing'.

Eat about 1.6 g protein per kg body weight per day, spread over 3-4 meals; extra protein above this gave no further measurable muscle gain (Morton 2018). This is the main thing that protects muscle while losing fat.

Keep the 15-minute home circuit as the fallback when the gym is impossible: training to near failure (RIR 1-3) gives most of the muscle benefit, so short, hard sets at home still count (Refalo 2023; Robinson 2024).

notes: Program data fix: 'Dumbbell overhead triceps extension' uses freeDbId 'Kettlebell_Overhead_Triceps_Extension', which has fewer than 2 images in free-exercise-db. Recommend switching it to 'Standing_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extension' (two-hand dumbbell overhead extension, 2 images).

Swaps with freeDbId null in the program (Outdoor brisk walk, Weighted plate crunch, Band face pull, Dumbbell swing, Farmer's march in place) can use: Trail_Running_Walking, Weighted_Crunches, Band_Pull_Apart (closest band rear-delt move), Vertical_Swing, Farmers_Walk respectively.
Carry pattern has thin coverage in free-exercise-db (only Farmers_Walk plus strongman sled/yoke items); carry alternates therefore include grip holds and sled work.
